newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end weaker, platinum up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end weaker, platinum up.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly slightly lower Wednesday, after two days of gains earlier this week, but platinum ended higher.

"Automobile production is looking healthy which supports demand for platinum group metals in emissions control devices, while demand for PGM's in semi-conductors is also good, but supply of the metals is plentiful," CPM Group analyst Edward Kemp said.
"Russian sales of PGMs for the year has probably already mostly occurred in the first half, despite rumors to the contrary," he said.
January platinum ended up $1.00 at $391.90 an ounce, after seeing a two week high intraday at $392.40.
December palladium ended down 75 cents at $120.00, after seeing a two week high Tuesday at $121.50.
The popular April platinum/April gold intermarket spread rose to $3.80 an ounce, from a three month low of $2.50 Monday.
"Long April platinum/short April gold (spreads) are being considered at current levels," Smith Barney Washington DC analyst Phil Tiger said.
COMEX December gold ended down 20 cents at $385.90 an ounce, after trading a narrow $386.30-385.40 range, inside Tuesday's wide range which included a two week high at $386.50.
"Fund shortcovering is starting but so far its only about 10-15 percent of the total position," Friedberg Mercantile Group's Toronto based analyst Chris Foster said.
Open interest in gold futures fell 6,210 lots Tuesday to 187,813, while silver open interest was down 947 lots at 94,098 lots.
Funds had built up a record net short position in recent months, according to the CFTC Commitment of Traders data, as spot gold bullion prices fell to an 18 month low.
In bullion trade Wednesday, spot gold ended quoted $383.60/384.10, from the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $383.50 and the New York close Tuesday at $383.90/384.40.
COMEX December silver ended ended down 20 cents at $4.988 an ounce, after popping above $5.000 to a session high at $5.010 for the first time in a week.
Seasonal holiday demand in India in the next few weeks and seasonal fabricator demand in Europe and the U.S. in the next few months should contribute to support for precious metals, analysts said.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
